scientific_findings: Actor-critic has higher mean value in all 12/12 profile × allowance groups; this is not uniform casewise dominance.
There are 1 paired cases where distillation is better, retained explicitly with identities and both values.
Actor-critic improves with allowance in both zero-explicit-price profiles, but its value is unchanged across allowances in both priced profiles.
Distillation value and expected action counts are unchanged for every matched seed/scenario across all three allowances; more fitting did not improve deployed outcomes in this grid.
Every 4-second distillation worker stops at the common 512-epoch ceiling before using the full CPU allowance; actor-critic workers instead stop cooperatively at the CPU allowance.
There are 0 matched cases whose actor value worsens when increasing allowance; this is descriptive, not a monotonic-improvement guarantee.
The successful repeat is the analysis source. First-attempt artifacts remain integrity-rejected and are not pooled, imputed, or used for checkpoint selection.
Known finite model and three training seeds; these observations do not establish general algorithm superiority, real-task transfer, equal total physical cost, or production adoption.
